title: Route correlation IDs, retrospective heatmaps, and sampled-context attachments for routing observability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add lightweight, stable correlation IDs for each user request and per-route decision span, attach sampled contextual blobs (late-binding annotations) to a bounded percentage of decision logs, and build a retrospective heatmap view that aggregates decision frequency and latency by region+tier+model-variant. Goal: make root-cause and cost investigations fast without blowing up storage or exposing PII. Scope includes ID generation, sampling rules, storage schema changes for sampled attachments, a batch job to build heatmaps, a UI surface in Console for the heatmap, and query endpoints for ad-hoc forensic analysis. Non-goal: full-fidelity capture of every request or unbounded tracing retention. This ticket focuses on instrumentation and the retrospective aggregation path; SDK changes and external integrations will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Every incoming API request is assigned a stable 16-byte correlation_id that appears on route-decision logs and traces
Sampling rules implement two knobs: deterministic client-based sampling (by customer ID) and stochastic global sampling with adjustable rate via Console
Attach sampled contextual blobs (<= 8KB) to at most 1% default of route-decision logs; attachments must be stored in compressed, encrypted blobs and linked from line-level logs
Heatmap batch job populates a daily aggregation table covering region x tier x model-variant with counts, p50/p95 latency, and token-cost estimates
Console has a heatmap view for a configurable time window and a drill-down link to a sampled decision log and full attachment when available
Instrumentation adds <5% tail latency overhead on the critical RPC path in staging and passes load tests with 2x expected traffic
Playbook for forensics includes an API to query decision traces by correlation_id and an automated runbook for suspected model-fallback incidents
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: flagged as high priority after two postmortems where region fallbacks were hard to trace. Assigned to Liam. (Maya)

2026-03-03 - Design sync: decided on 16-byte base64 correlation_id (stable across retries) and a separate span_id for per-hop tracing. We will avoid propagating raw user prompt in attachments; instead store redacted/hashed prompt metadata and a pointer to encrypted attachment. (Liam, Priya)

2026-03-05 - Trade-off: storing attachments inline in the log was simpler but would increase ES index size drastically. Chose external encrypted blobstore (S3/GCS) + compact pointer in log. Leads to additional operational cost but keeps search performance. (Eng)

2026-03-07 - Implementation note: added middleware in router service to stamp correlation_id and sampling_decision early. Sampling decision is computed from (customer_id hash mod 10000) < floor(rate*100). This ensures deterministic client-sampled traces for a given customer. (Diego)

2026-03-09 - Perf: microbench shows <2% median overhead when not sampling and ~8% CPU increase when attachment compression happens. We'll gate attachment compression with a worker pool to avoid blocking request threads. (Perf team)
2026-03-10 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6143 implements correlation_id, sampling flags, and blob pointers. Needs security review for attachment encryption. (Liam)

2026-03-11 - Security review: KMS envelope encryption accepted; ensure attachments are scanned for PII before blob persist. Added a small redaction pipeline to drop long sequences and email patterns. (Security)

2026-03-12 - QA plan: run canary on staging->region-us-west2 for 48h at 0.5% global sampling, validate Console heatmap generation on synthetic traffic, and run para-load to ensure tail latencies under SLA. (QA)

Follow-ups: SDK propagation of correlation_id, longer-term retention tier for sampled attachments, and an opt-out control for customers that cannot have attachments stored. These will be separate tickets.
